stmt_text: Prove by mathematical induction that 5^{2n+1} + 2^{2n+1} is divisible by 7 for any integer n \ge 1.
sol_text:
Model answer:
Step 1. n = 1: 5^3 + 2^3 = 125 + 8 = 133 = 7 \times 19. True.
Step 2. Assume true for n = k: 5^{2k+1} + 2^{2k+1} = 7M for some integer M.
Step 3. 5^{2k+3} + 2^{2k+3} = 25 \times 5^{2k+1} + 4 \times 2^{2k+1} = 25\left(7M - 2^{2k+1}\right) + 4 \times 2^{2k+1} = 175M - 21 \times 2^{2k+1} = 7\left(25M - 3 \times 2^{2k+1}\right), which is divisible by 7.
So if true for n = k it is true for n = k + 1; since true for n = 1, by induction it is true for all n \ge 1.
